column1: # deferred.tsv - the requirement rows milestone 1 does not prove, and why.
# RegistryTests.AccountsForEveryM1Row is M1's gate (docs/DESIGN.md section 7): every row of
# RFC 9110, RFC 9112, RFC 9113, RFC 7541 and RFC 6585 in requirements.tsv is either named by a
# test ([Requirement]) or matched by a rule here. A row's reason is the FIRST rule that matches it,
# so narrow rules come before broad ones. Stale rules fail the gate: one naming an exact id
# that a test proves, and one that is the first match of no unproven row (it defers nothing).
# Columns (tab-separated): match (a row id, or a glob with * over ids), actor (empty: any),
# keyword (empty: any), milestone (where the work belongs), reason.
#   M2      TLS 1.3 (and TLS in general: ALPN, SNI, https, closure alerts)
#   M4      QUIC + HTTP/3, and server push, built once for HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 (their shared
#   M5      the .NET interfaces: the HttpClient handler is the full client (HTTP/2, redirects,
#           credentials, retries, pipelining, user-agent behavior); M1's C ABI client is one
#           blocking HTTP/1.1 connection that sends what its caller writes
#   M6      the roles and extensions "complete" is decided to include (docs/DESIGN.md section 1,
#           open): proxies, gateways, tunnels, caches, priorities, protocol upgrades
#   app     semantics a server library hands to its application (the handler decides them:
#           methods, representations, validators, conditions, ranges, authentication), or that
#           a client's caller decides (what a request carries); proven, if ever, by the
#   option  a MAY or OPTIONAL this library does not take (the reason says what it does instead)
#   design  met by construction, with nothing a test could observe (the reason says where)
#   spec    addressed to authors of specifications or registrations, not to implementations
